text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are powerful tools: they can answer questions, summarise texts and help with writing. However, they also have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, and their knowledge stops at a certain date. For these reasons, it is always wise to check important facts yourself.
